title: Board Book Navigation — Usability Evaluation Report
feature: Board book document navigation (Version 1 Full width · Version 2 Floating controls · Version 3 Reading mode)
method: Synthetic Persona Usability Study | NN/G Methodology | 4 Personas | 10 User Stories | 3 Variants
disclaimer: All results come from simulated think-aloud sessions with synthetic personas. Numbers are simulated, not measured user data, and must be validated with real users.
context: Prototype at localhost:5173/board-book-page-nav.html with the real Q4 board pack (5 agenda items, 6 documents, 7 pages). Platform constraint: continuous scroll works only within one document; nothing can be added inside the document, so moving to the next document is possible only through the viewer's navigation panels ('next page' on the last page, the document dropdown, keyboard ← →). State evaluated: after the 4 Must-fix items from the design review. Re-run 2026-10-22: Version 2 was replaced by the former Version 4 (bottom page pill with previous / next document, zoom card left, annotation palette right, agenda open, phone 'Document tools' sheet); its column was re-simulated with the same personas and stories. Since 2026-10-19 all versions also lost the '← → pages' keyboard hint (the keys still work) and got the Figma Search / Ask AI panels; V1 / V3 ratings were not re-simulated. Re-run 2026-10-23: the reading-progress bar was removed from Version 3, and Version 3 was re-rated in its current state (|< / >| document buttons in the bottom bar, no progress) with the same rules as the new Version 2, so both are compared as built. Product decision 2026-10-23: in every version the agenda is open by default and the phone tools open from the same 'Document tools' (dots) sheet. US04 and the phone story were re-rated on that basis (V1 / V3 prototypes do not implement it yet).

variants.name: V1 Full width
variants.summary: Top toolbar: TOC toggle · document dropdown · page input N / 7 with ⌄ next / ⌃ previous · tools. Vertical zoom card on the left. Agenda closed by default. Below 768px tools collapse into ⋯.

variants.name: V2 Floating controls
variants.summary: Agenda open beside the document (collapses while Search / Ask AI is open below 1800px). Top bar: agenda toggle · document dropdown · download / search / Ask AI. One floating view card left (+ % − | fit width · fullscreen, icon buttons with tooltips), annotation palette right (draw, highlight, comment). One bottom pill: |< previous document · ‹ [N] / 7 › · next document >| with 'Previous / Next document: <name>' tooltips. Phone (<768px): the cards fold into one 'Document tools' button (6 dots) opening a labelled DS bottom sheet (Zoom − % +, Fit to width, Fit to page, Actual size, Fullscreen, Annotate, Add comment). Re-simulated 2026-10-22.

variants.name: V3 Reading mode
variants.summary: Top bar: TOC toggle · document dropdown · search / download / Ask AI. Always-visible bottom bar: |< previous document · ‹ N / 7 › · next document >| · zoom − % + · fit width · focus mode · highlight / comment (zoom, fit, focus and annotation tools in ⋯ below 768px). Agenda closed by default. No reading-progress bar (removed 2026-10-23). Re-rated 2026-10-23 in this state.

goals.text: Assess orientation: can each persona tell which document and page they are on (H1 visibility of system status).
Identify breakdown moments at document boundaries under the one-document-at-a-time constraint.
Evaluate control placement: travel distance from the point of reading to the 'continue' action, per variant.
Measure cognitive load of each layout (number of control zones, icon-only actions, hidden affordances).
Quantify simulated task success and SEQ per user story, persona and variant.

stories.text: As a reader, I want to see which document and page I am on, so I don't lose my place.
As a reader, I want to read a document page by page without hunting for controls.
As a reader, I want to continue to the next document when I reach the end of the current one.
As a reader, I want to jump straight to the documents of a specific agenda item.
As a reader, I want to go to a page number someone mentions in the meeting.
As a reader, I want to zoom or fit a dense table so I can read the figures.
As a reader, I want to highlight or comment on a passage to discuss it later.
As a reader, I want to search the board book for a term.
As a reader, I want to read comfortably on a tablet or phone.
As a reader, I want to go back to the previous document.

personas.name: Margaret Chen
personas.goal: Check the final board pack end to end before it goes to directors.
personas.mentalModel: Keyboard shortcuts, dense toolbars, Notion/Acrobat-like patterns.
personas.risk: Impatient with extra steps; skims past labels.

personas.name: David Okafor
personas.goal: Review the pack and annotate items that need the Chair's attention.
personas.mentalModel: Explicit toolbar buttons and labelled Next / Previous.
personas.risk: Hesitates when something changes without explanation.
personas.emotion: Cautious; fears missing a document in a legal pack.

personas.name: Patricia Reyes
personas.goal: Open the pack and read the documents for one agenda item.
personas.mentalModel: A visible, labelled button for every action; step by step.
personas.risk: Ignores icon-only controls; never opens ⋯ menus.

personas.name: Robert Hale
personas.goal: Read the pack on iPad the evening before the meeting and mark questions.
personas.mentalModel: Reading app: swipe or tap to turn pages, everything within thumb reach.
personas.risk: No keyboard; low patience for admin-style UI.
personas.emotion: Time-poor; wants the right document fast.

MC.scenario: Opens the pack to spot-check the cover.
MC.behaviour: Reads the dropdown and N / 7 instantly in all variants.
MC.friction: V2/V3: document name (top bar) and page (bottom bar) sit far apart.

MC.scenario: Finishes 'Opening, quorum, and minutes' and wants the CEO report.
MC.behaviour: Presses → on the keyboard; the next document loads.
MC.friction: None for her — the keyboard hint tells her ← → works. No friction: → on the keyboard (the on-screen hint is gone, she knows the keys) or >| in the pill.

MC.scenario: Jumps to item 4 to verify the audit motion wording.
MC.behaviour: Agenda is open by default in every version: clicks the document in the agenda list.
MC.friction: None — agenda open by default (product decision 2026-10-23).
V2/V3: the page field is in the bottom bar; she looks at the top first.

MC.scenario: Checks the cash-flow table on page 5.
MC.friction: V2: the card now shows 'Fit' when fitted, so the old '100%' confusion is gone.

MC.behaviour: Picks Highlight; V3 she also looks for Draw.

DO.scenario: Opens the pack on the cover.
DO.behaviour: Reads 'Cover and agenda.pdf' and '1 / 7' and assumes the cover has 7 pages.
DO.friction: Global counter next to a single-document view (all variants); no variant shows progress any more.

DO.scenario: Reaches the bottom of 'Opening, quorum, and minutes'.
DO.behaviour: Scrolls, nothing more appears; thinks the pack failed to load. V1: finds ⌄ at the top, unsure it means 'next document'. V2: clicks › beside the sheet. V3: › is right under where he stopped.
DO.friction: Silent document end; 'Next page' tooltip never says a new document opens. V2: the bottom pill is right under where he stopped; >| names the next document on hover. Still nothing in the page itself.
V2: zoom and view are still two cards, but 'Fit' / '%' make the state clear.

DO.scenario: Comments on the retention bonus pool.
DO.behaviour: Selects Comment and clicks the sheet.
DO.friction: No confirmation that the comment pin was saved (all variants).

DO.scenario: Wants to re-check the previous document.
DO.friction: V1: ⌃ reads as 'collapse', not 'previous document'. V2: |< 'Previous document' sits next to ‹ in the pill.

PR.scenario: Opens the pack for the first time.
PR.behaviour: Scans for words; finds the document name but not what the number means.
PR.friction: V2: controls in three places (left card, right palette, bottom pill) — fewer than before, still icon-only.

PR.scenario: Reads the CEO report page by page.
PR.behaviour: Looks for a 'next' button. V1: thinks ⌄ opens a list. V2: big round › is obvious. V3: › in the bottom bar.
PR.friction: V1: vertical chevrons look like dropdown toggles. V2: ‹ › in the bottom pill are small (28px) but where she expects them.

PR.scenario: Gets to the end of the minutes document.
PR.behaviour: V1: believes the pack has ended and stops. V2/V3: notices the › arrow after a pause and tries it.
PR.friction: Nothing signals that more documents follow; V1's continue control is far away at the top. V2/V3: the continue control is in the right place, but |< / >| are icon-only and their names need hover.

PR.scenario: Needs the Audit committee report for item 4.
PR.behaviour: Agenda is open by default in every version: clicks the document in the agenda list.
PR.friction: None — agenda open by default (product decision 2026-10-23).

PR.scenario: The financial table is too small.
PR.friction: V1: icon-only card; V3: '− 100% +' reads clearly. V2: '+ 100% −' in the left card reads clearly, as in V3.

PR.scenario: Opens the pack on her phone.
PR.behaviour: Every version opens its tools from the same 'Document tools' (dots) sheet; rows are labelled once open.
PR.friction: The dots trigger is icon-only, so she hesitates to open it (all versions).

DIR.scenario: Opens the pack on iPad the night before.
DIR.behaviour: Wants to know how much is left.
DIR.friction: No variant shows how much is left; V2/V3 show the counter in the bottom bar.

DIR.scenario: Finishes the CEO report, wants the financials.
DIR.behaviour: No keyboard. V1: has to reach the top toolbar. V2: taps › beside the sheet. V3: taps › in the bottom bar (thumb zone).
DIR.friction: V1: continue control outside thumb reach and unlabeled. V2/V3: › and >| in the bottom pill, in the thumb zone.

DIR.scenario: Goes straight to the audit committee report.
DIR.behaviour: Agenda is open by default in every version: clicks the document in the agenda list.
DIR.friction: None — agenda open by default (product decision 2026-10-23).

DIR.scenario: Marks a question on the auditor fee.
DIR.friction: Icon-only tools; tooltips don't show on touch.
V2: on iPad portrait (768–1023) the two cards stay in the side gutters beside the sheet — no overlap, a little visual noise.

shared: The end of a document is silent in every variant: nothing below the last page and the 'next' control is labelled 'Next page', so no persona is told that another document follows.
The global counter 'N / 7' sits next to a single-document view, so David and Patricia misread how long the current document is.
All navigation and tool controls are icon-only (incl. V2's |< >| and its 6-dot 'Document tools' button); tooltips need hover, so they don't help Patricia or Robert on iPad.

divergent.PR: V1: gives up; V2/V3: finds › / >| in the bottom bar after a pause
divergent.DIR: Needs thumb reach — V2/V3 bottom bar

divergent.DO: V2: two cards remain, 'Fit' label helps

divergent.PR: Hesitates at the icon-only dots trigger

heuristics.name: Visibility of system status
heuristics.evidence: Document end is silent; global N / 7 misread as document length (US01, US03).

heuristics.name: Match with the real world
heuristics.evidence: V1 ⌄ / ⌃ read as dropdown/collapse, not page turns (US02, US10).

heuristics.name: User control and freedom
heuristics.evidence: Previous page on the first page returns to the previous document; Esc leaves focus mode.

heuristics.name: Consistency and standards
heuristics.evidence: V1 uses ⌄⌃, V2/V3 ‹ › for pages and |< >| for documents; zoom % still means different things in V3 on phones (US06).

heuristics.name: Recognition rather than recall
heuristics.evidence: Icon-only controls, agenda behind an unlabeled icon, tools in ⋯ on mobile (US04, US09).

heuristics.name: Flexibility and efficiency
heuristics.evidence: Keyboard ← → crosses documents; page field accepts direct input (US03, US05).

heuristics.name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
heuristics.evidence: V2 now uses three zones (view card, palette, bottom pill) and one button on phones; V3 consolidates everything in one bar.

heuristics.name: Help users recover from errors
heuristics.evidence: When Patricia believes the pack ended, nothing helps her recover (US03, V1).

issues.issue: Document end is silent and the only way on is a control labelled 'Next page'
issues.impact: Patricia stops reading in V1; David hesitates

issues.issue: V1 places next/previous in the top toolbar with vertical ⌄ / ⌃ icons
issues.impact: Far from the reading end point; icons misread

issues.issue: Global counter 'N / 7' beside a single-document view
issues.impact: Wrong sense of document length and position

issues.issue: Icon-only navigation and tools (incl. V2 |< >|); tooltips need hover
Agenda closed by default behind an unlabeled sidebar icon — resolved: open by default in every version (product decision 2026-10-23)
issues.impact: Patricia can't jump to an agenda item's documents

issues.issue: V2 spreads controls over three zones; on tablet (768–1023) the cards stay in the gutters beside the sheet
issues.impact: Scanning cost; some clutter at the sheet edges

issues.issue: Zoom % meaning differs (V3 '54%' default on phone); V2 now shows 'Fit' when fitted
Mobile: tools behind an icon-only trigger — now one labelled 'Document tools' sheet in every version, but the dots trigger itself is unlabeled
issues.impact: Patricia never finds Highlight on the phone

issues.issue: V3 focus-mode icon (⌃⌄ 'expand') is ambiguous — fixed 2026-10-20: arrow-resize-diagonal, moved to the bottom bar

recommendations.title: Make the document boundary visible inside the navigation panel
recommendations.fix: On the last page of a document the next control becomes a labelled DS Button 'Next document: <name> ›' (and 'Previous document' on the first page); tooltip says the same.
recommendations.status: V3, 2026-10-20: partly done — ‹‹ / ›› buttons with 'Previous / Next document: <name>' tooltips are in the bottom bar; not re-tested

recommendations.title: Use V3's bottom bar as the primary navigation location
recommendations.fix: Keep ‹ N / 7 › at the bottom where reading ends; in V1 replace ⌄ / ⌃ with ‹ ›.

recommendations.title: Show local and global position
recommendations.fix: 'Page 1 of 2 · 4 / 7' in the counter; document name next to it.

recommendations.title: Label the primary actions
recommendations.fix: Text labels on Previous / Next at ≥1024px; persistent labels instead of hover-only tooltips on touch.

recommendations.title: Open the agenda by default on wide screens
recommendations.fix: In V3 open the agenda panel by default at ≥1280px (as V2 does), with a labelled toggle 'Agenda'.
recommendations.status: Adopted 2026-10-23: agenda open by default in every version

recommendations.title: Align zoom semantics and label the mobile menu
recommendations.fix: Show 'Fit' when fitted (done in V2); 100% = sheet's natural width; label the mobile tools trigger ('More tools' / 'Tools') — V2's sheet already labels every row.

recommendations.title: Carry V2's phone sheet to tablet portrait and to V3
recommendations.fix: Use the labelled 'Document tools' bottom sheet below 1024px (not only below 768px) and in V3's mobile bar instead of ⋯; give the trigger a text label.
recommendations.status: Adopted 2026-10-23: the dots 'Document tools' sheet is the phone pattern for every version

phases.name: Phase 1 — Validation
phases.text: After sprint 1, re-test I-01…I-05 fixes on V3 and the new V2 with the same persona types.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Breadth
phases.text: Add iPad and phone tasks; recruit 2 real users per persona type (incl. 2 directors).

phases.name: Phase 3 — Longitudinal
phases.text: Learnability over 3 meeting cycles; diary study with directors reading packs at home.

questions: Do directors read packs linearly or jump by agenda item?
Is a labelled 'Next document' enough, or do readers expect the next document to load automatically?
How often do readers need the previous document mid-meeting?
Which share of readers uses the keyboard at all?
Do readers miss a 'how much is left' signal now that no variant shows reading progress?

takeaways: With the agenda open by default and the same phone sheet in every version, Version 3 leads again: its single control zone is the difference that remains.
Version 2 is a close second — same bottom-bar navigation, but three control zones on desktop.
The document boundary is the critical moment — the fix belongs in the navigation panel, not the document.
Labels and position (local + global) matter more than more controls.
Validate with real directors on iPad before committing — the gap is small and the study is simulated.
